question: Why did facility FAC-011 report a stockout of ORS sachet in 2026-03?

evidence_for_hypotheses.h1_late_order: Order was placed on 2026-02-05, five days before the cutoff of 2026-02-10, so it is not late; delivery month matches expectation and no slip occurred.
evidence_for_hypotheses.h2_supplier_underfill: Facility fill rate (0.959) exceeds county average (0.910); relative shortfall is negative, indicating no under‑fill by the supplier.
evidence_for_hypotheses.h3_payment_arrears: County shows arrears in 2026-02 (3,000,000 KES) but not flagged as major; a slight drop in fill rate (-0.0105) is observed versus the prior month.
evidence_for_hypotheses.h4_demand_surge: Consumption this month (536) is 72.2% higher than the 3‑month average (311.33), indicating a demand surge.
evidence_for_hypotheses.h5_record_error: Computed closing stock (0) matches reported closing (0); identity holds and reported 8 stock‑out days are plausible—no record error detected.
evidence_for_hypotheses.h6_expiry: Wastage this month is 0 and average wastage over three months is 0; no expiry‑related loss detected.
evidence_for_hypotheses.h7_national_disruption: County fill rate dropped slightly (-0.0105) and no synthetic web notice related to a national disruption was found.

data_analyst.analysis_summary: The evidence shows that the only notable anomaly for FAC-011 in March 2026 is a sharp increase in ORS sachet consumption (72% above the 3‑month average), indicating a demand surge. All other examined factors—order timing, supplier fill rates, payment arrears magnitude, record integrity, wastage, and national disruption signals—show no supporting evidence for the stockout.

H1.reasoning: Order placed 5 days before the cutoff (orders#1505) and delivery occurred as scheduled; no late order or delivery slip.

H2.reasoning: Facility fill rate (0.9591) exceeds county average (0.9096); underfill flag is false (orders#1505).

H3.reasoning: Arrears exist but amount owed (3M KES) is far below the 30M threshold; county fill drop is minimal and major arrears flag is false.

H4.reasoning: Consumption this month (536) is 72.16% higher than the 3‑month average (311.33), surpassing the 25% surge threshold (stock#1506).

H5.reasoning: Closing balance matches, identity holds, and reported stockout days (8) are plausible; no discrepancy detected (stock#1506).

H6.reasoning: Wastage this month is zero, matching the 3‑month average; high wastage condition not met (stock#1506).

H7.reasoning: County fill dropped slightly but no public web notice of disruption was found.

data_limitations: Analysis limited to a single month (2026-03) and one facility.
Computed evidence does not include qualitative factors (e.g., local disease outbreaks) that could explain demand spikes.
Payment arrears data lacks county‑wide financial context beyond the 30M threshold.
Web notice search may miss non‑indexed or offline announcements.

theories.title: Order placed after cutoff causing delivery delay
theories.mechanism: If the facility submits its order after the monthly cutoff, the supplier’s schedule pushes the shipment to the following month, leaving a period with no inbound stock and creating a gap that can lead to a stockout.
evidence_needed: Order timestamp recorded after the official cutoff date
Delivery receipt date falling in the month after the order
Inventory log showing zero on‑hand balance between order cutoff and next delivery
disconfirming_evidence: Delivery received in the same month as the order
Continuous positive on‑hand balance throughout the month
predictions: Stockout days coincide with the interval between cutoff and next delivery
The following month shows a receipt of the delayed order and a rebound in stock levels
Consumption patterns remain unchanged during the gap

theories.title: Supplier delivered less than requested relative to peers
theories.mechanism: When the supplier ships a quantity that is materially lower than the facility’s request—especially compared with peer facilities in the same supply cycle—the facility’s inventory depletes faster than anticipated, potentially reaching zero before the next replenishment.
evidence_needed: Delivery quantity for FAC‑011 lower than the ordered quantity
Fill rate for FAC‑011 noticeably below the county average for the same cycle
Peer facilities receiving a higher proportion of their orders in the same period
disconfirming_evidence: FAC‑011 fill rate equal to or higher than peers
Delivery quantity matches the order amount
No discrepancy between ordered and received units
predictions: Post‑delivery inventory shows a shortfall relative to forecast
Complaints or notes in supplier communication flag an under‑fill for this facility
Other facilities in the county maintain adequate stock while FAC‑011 experiences a stockout

theories.title: County arrears trigger supplier delivery reduction
theories.mechanism: If the county owes the supplier >=30 M KES, the supplier may curtail or delay shipments county‑wide as a credit control measure, reducing the volume that reaches each facility and increasing the risk of stockouts.
evidence_needed: Financial records confirming county‑wide arrears of at least 30 M KES at the time of the stockout
Correspondence from the supplier indicating reduced deliveries due to non‑payment
A measurable drop in county‑wide fill rates during the period in question
disconfirming_evidence: Arrears amount well below the 30 M KES threshold
Supplier statements confirming normal delivery schedules
County fill rates remain stable or improve despite arrears
predictions: Multiple facilities within the county report simultaneous stockouts
Delivery logs show reduced quantities for all facilities compared with previous cycles
Media or internal memos reference payment‑related supply constraints

theories.title: Unexpected demand spike exhausts stock
theories.mechanism: A sudden increase in consumption—exceeding 25 % above the three‑month average—drains the existing inventory faster than the scheduled replenishment can replace it, leading to a stockout before the next order arrives.
evidence_needed: Consumption data for March 2026 showing >25 % increase over the 3‑month average (e.g., 72 % rise)
Stock cards indicating rapid depletion of on‑hand balance during the month
No corresponding increase in order quantity for the same period
disconfirming_evidence: Inventory levels remaining stable despite reported usage
An order placed that matches the surge in consumption
predictions: High daily issue counts for ORS sachets early in the month
Stockout days clustered after the peak consumption period
Subsequent ordering patterns show a larger quantity to replenish the unexpected drawdown

theories.title: Data recording error mislabels stockout
theories.mechanism: If the stockout days were entered incorrectly—due to transcription mistakes or misapplied formulas—the system may flag a stockout even though physical stock never reached zero, creating a false alarm.
evidence_needed: Audit of the original stock‑card entries revealing a positive balance on the days marked as stockout
Reconciliation of the stock identity equation that shows no zero‑balance condition
Independent physical count confirming stock was on hand
disconfirming_evidence: Verified stock cards and electronic records both show zero balance on the reported days
Third‑party verification (e.g., supervisory visit) confirms the stockout
predictions: A re‑audit corrects the stockout count to zero days
No surge in consumption or ordering activity associated with the alleged stockout
Facility staff report no experience of stock shortage during the period

theories.title: Large expiry or damage write‑off depletes usable stock
theories.mechanism: When a substantial portion of the inventory is written off due to expiry, damage, or other loss, the usable stock quantity drops sharply, potentially leaving the facility without any usable units even if total stock appears sufficient on paper.
evidence_needed: Wastage logs showing a spike in expiry or damage entries for ORS sachets in the month preceding the stockout
Disposal records confirming the quantity removed from usable stock
A decline in the usable‑balance column of the stock register despite stable total balance
disconfirming_evidence: Wastage entries remain at baseline levels (e.g., zero or negligible)
No recorded expiries or damages for ORS sachets in the relevant period
predictions: A sudden drop in the usable‑on‑hand figure immediately before the stockout
Corresponding increase in waste‑related paperwork or disposal receipts
No change in consumption patterns; the shortage is driven by loss rather than demand

theories.title: Nationwide supply chain disruption limits deliveries
theories.mechanism: A country‑wide event—such as a tender failure, major logistics breakdown, or a public notice of supply interruption—reduces the volume of commodities dispatched to all counties, causing simultaneous stockouts at facilities that rely on the central distribution system.
evidence_needed: Official public notice, media report, or supplier announcement of a national supply disruption during the relevant timeframe
County‑wide data showing a uniform drop in fill rates or delivery volumes
Multiple facilities across the county reporting stockouts for the same product in the same month
disconfirming_evidence: Absence of any national‑level announcement or media coverage of disruption
Other counties or facilities continuing to receive normal deliveries
County fill rates remaining consistent with historical levels
predictions: Synchronized stockout reports from several facilities within the county
Supplier shipment manifests indicating reduced total quantities dispatched nationally
Logistics records showing delays or cancellations of transport trips for the period
